name: hash-sha1-stream
algorithm: std SHA-1 through the streaming state, fed 1,500-byte pieces (the last piece is the remainder) of splitmix64 bytes, one fresh state per pass, reps passes with a one-byte write-back (mk/hash-sha1-stream.mk).

skip.c: no std hash: C has no standard SHA-1; OpenSSL's portable C is a third-party library, and no third-party code stands in (plan/06-m6.md 4.1)
skip.rust: no std SHA-1: Rust std has none (only SipHash-1-3 in DefaultHasher); the sha1 crate is third-party, and no crate stands in (plan/06-m6.md 4.1)

notes: Idiomatic standard library, the streaming case: Mk Sha1State.New/Bytes/Sum, Go crypto/sha1.New, Write per piece, Sum, Zig init/update/final. 1,500 is not a multiple of the block, so the partial-block path of Bytes runs on every piece. Bytes per second = mib * 1048576 * reps / median. Both checksums equal hash-sha1's (the same digests; the write-back sequence repeats, so 40 and 48 passes fold to one value).

Go: crypto/sha1 uses the SHA extensions (sha1rnds4) or AVX2 on amd64 when the CPU has them, whatever GOAMD64 says (run-time dispatch in the library); Mk's Sha1 is scalar on every CPU (D8-17 builds only SHA-256's instructions), as Zig's at x86_64_v2 is. Labelled: on a CPU with the SHA extensions the go cell compares instruction sets as well as libraries (status/std-hash2.md, H2-5).

Checksums from the go column (GOAMD64=v2 -pgo=off, Go 1.27.3, owner's machine, 2026-11-12); the Mk (mk build --release) and Zig 0.17.0 (-O ReleaseFast -mcpu=x86_64_v2) columns printed the same in `go run ./tools/bench verify -publish-size` (status/std-hash2.md, fix round). Written by the std-hash2 lane for review finding H2-8. Not published: no number here is a measurement.
